violations.why: timerCount++ in Timer_A is non-atomic; Timer_B (equal priority) can preempt and set it, and the increment overwrites it.
Higher-priority Timer_C can write between the read and write of the increment.
Reset ISR can zero timerCount between the increment's read and write; the reset is lost.
Force ISR's increment can be lost when it preempts Timer_A's read-modify-write.
Reset can change timerCount after the increment, so the check at line 97 sees a different value.
Timer_C can overwrite timerCount between the increment and the check.
Timer_B can overwrite timerCount between the increment and the check.
Force ISR increments timerCount between the write and the check, so the ==1 test fails.
Timer_A (equal priority) can modify timerCount between Timer_B's write and its check.
Force ISR can increment timerCount before the check at line 111.
Timer_C can write timerCount between line 109 and the check.
Reset can zero timerCount before the check at line 111.
Higher-priority Reset can preempt Timer_C and zero timerCount before the check.
Timer_C can preempt Force's non-atomic increment, and its write is overwritten.
Reset can preempt Force's increment, and the stale increment overwrites the reset.
